data.rationale: sciCORE provides Apptainer, NOT Docker -- its docs say you can use Apptainer to download and run docker images from public registries, so a Docker image is a valid SOURCE (apptainer pull docker://...) but `docker run` is unavailable there. The reason to prefer a container over the uv-sync venv is MEASURED: that venv is 56,717 files / 5.45 GB. GPFS is a parallel filesystem -- strong on large streaming reads, weak on metadata storms -- and every concurrently-running array task walks that tree on import; at a throttle of 20 that is a metadata storm on shared storage. A .sif is ONE read-only memory-mapped file, which is the access pattern the filesystem is good at. It also removes 'compute nodes have no internet' by construction. The image carries DEPENDENCIES ONLY: the repo is private and the image is not, so baking code in would force a private registry and an authenticated pull on every node, whereas a public PyPI-only image needs no credentials anywhere (which also sidesteps the token problem); and code changes hourly while dependencies change monthly, so the checkout is bind-mounted and `git pull` is the whole update. Run with --cleanenv so a stray host PYTHONPATH cannot shadow the image, which means the BLAS/OpenMP thread pins must be passed in explicitly via APPTAINERENV_*. Files: containers/Dockerfile, scripts/cluster/pull_container.sh, app/services/slurm_array.py::_runtime_block. The venv route still works and is the fallback.
data.title: Cluster runs use an Apptainer .sif, not a venv and not Docker

data.rationale: Both variants build from one containers/Dockerfile via --build-arg VARIANT=cpu|cuda. MEASURED sizes: CPU 2.8 GB docker -> 620 MB .sif; CUDA 9.78 GB -> 3.28 GB .sif; the venv it replaces is 5.45 GB across 56,717 files. CPU is VERIFIED on WSL2 running the real code: --cleanenv isolation holds, thread pins survive it via APPTAINERENV_*, the repo imports from the bind mount (not baked in), and a real manifest is generated. That is the SLURM path, done. GPU is a GENUINE NEGATIVE: torch.cuda.is_available() is False inside the container even with --nv and /usr/lib/wsl/lib bound. WSL2 routes CUDA through a driver shim that --nv does not pick up. This is a WSL limitation and says nothing about sciCORE GPU partitions, where --nv is the standard mechanism -- but it does mean WSL is NOT a valid proxy for testing the GPU path. The array template passes --nv only when gpus>0; without it a GPU job silently runs on CPU inside an allocation billed as GPU, which is the most expensive way to be wrong.
data.title: Apptainer CPU container verified end-to-end; GPU fails on WSL2 specifically

data.rationale: auto_merge.py:79-104 enqueues one merge job per staging file and store_merge.py:8-11 takes the master lock per DATA PIECE (non-blocking, so the web app is never blocked). That is N_files x N_pieces lock/open/flush cycles on a 584 MB file. Merge throughput is ~constant while production scales with machine count, so producers outpace the drain and STAGING_DIR grows unbounded with no signal. Fix: one lock acquisition, one dst open, MANY sources -- but BOUNDED by max_files/max_bytes/max_seconds, because an unbounded drain starves readers and recreates D5 (cross-process readers hard-fail while a writer holds the lock). Staging files are deleted ONLY after the dst is closed and flushed (deleting inside the loop then crashing destroys results). Per-file failure isolation; explicit (finished_at, run_id) ordering so last-writer-wins is a decision not an artefact of hostname sort order; backpressure (remaining not shrinking across passes) surfaced in the UI. Plan 13.
data.title: Multi-machine writes reach the master via a BOUNDED batch drain, not one file at a time

data.rationale: Our pipeline thresholded RAW dF/F. The AnimalClass reference thresholds dF/F that has been low-pass filtered AND linearly detrended. Measured on DON-006084/20210519/S1 (404x55740 @ 30.9668 Hz): raw dF/F with 2sigma/7fr gave 92.0% silent; my 7->3 change gave 0.0% silent at 17x the corpus median rate; the reference's OWN parameters applied to raw dF/F silence 100% of cells. A plain 2sigma threshold on filtered+detrended input reproduces the reference EXACTLY (43 events, same as reference). A 2-D sweep is flat across the entire grid once the input is right. Ground truth: 520 legacy sessions store both F_detrended.npy and F_upphase.npy; re-running the recipe reproduces stored output at 100.0000% frame agreement on 4 of 5 sessions. BOTH my 7->3 change AND the original 7 were wrong. Two briefing facts were also wrong: min_width_event_upphase is 10 not 7 (reassigned at line ~499, confirmed empirically - shortest event is exactly 10 frames in all 16 sampled sessions), and min_thresh_std_upphase=1.5 is DEAD CODE, commented out at both call sites.
data.title: The binarization bug was the INPUT, not the threshold or the width

data.rationale: run_corpus_campaign.py's _SUITE2P_DRIVER called select_functional_channel, used the result for the fps lookup, PRINTED it, then called run_suite2p_munit(mesc, munit, fps, out) with a bare int and no functional_chan - so the callee re-resolved with functional_chan=None and fell back to the LOWEST channel. Silent: it produces a plausible run on the wrong pixels rather than an error. Measured over 22 finished runs: 1 wrong (DON-009191/20220215/MUnit_0 read Channel_0, a flat constant 1636, while Channel_1 has std 118.10), 19 agreed BY LUCK because their correct channel IS the lowest, 2 had no h5py_key at all. The crash signature is ValueError 'Maximum allowed size exceeded' in bin_movie - batch_size=0 because a flat channel leaves zero good frames after registration. FIX: pass the RECORD not the int, and verify h5py_key read back from db.npy matches the chosen channel before ingesting - an argument assertion cannot catch an entry point that accepts the record and ignores it.
data.title: The campaign computed the functional channel and then discarded it

Six consumers derive from it and only from it: catalog param parsing (unknown params 400, never ignored), the WHERE/SELECT builder in metadata_store.query_sessions, facet counting, the <ba-filter> client which renders from GET /api/datasets/catalog/schema and ships no field list, the Data-Wrangler column-stats panel and Excel-style header filters on /overview, and the mandatory ? popover. Adding a queryable variable is ONE registry entry plus a migration: no route change, no SQL edit, no UI change, no client release. Rejected information_schema reflection because it cannot supply a label, control type, facet decision or help text and would expose internal columns; reflection is kept only as a test that fails when a sessions/recordings/animals column has no FIELDS entry and no explicit exclusion, so a migration cannot outrun the registry.

data.rationale: suite2p_run.py called cells_only(raw), dropping iscell==0 rows, and write_fluor_step stored the subset with NO roi_ids beside it. Two live corruptions were already in the store: DON-017117/20231113/S1 version bd242aebc8d7 has 128 rows against 131 curated ROIs (unrecoverable), and 2 of 36 QC partitions are stale - one with 230 QC rows for 172 ROIs, MORE rows than cells exist. FIX: write_fluor_step emits fluorescence/<version>/roi_ids in the SAME call as the array so they cannot drift apart, and refuses a step whose ids contradict ids already stored at that version. Full-extent-plus-mask was rejected: DON-017115/20231113/S1 keeps 309 of 930 ROIs, so full extent would inflate it ~3x on the binding constraint. roi_id ALWAYS means the suite2p ROI index within the subsession, never a positional index.

data.rationale: Array tasks are isolated and write their own outputs, so nothing on the cluster needs Postgres, Redis or Docker -- and the code already agrees: every accessor in basic_analysis/io/services.py returns None rather than raising when a service is absent, and callers fall through to the HDF5/filesystem tier. scripts/cluster/bootstrap_remote.sh therefore WRITES a cluster-local docker/.env with PG_ENABLED=0 and REDIS_ENABLED=0, and the container image bakes the same values. The point is to make the degradation a DECISION rather than an accident: unset, a job could wait on a connection that was never going to exist, and the degradation chain is designed to make exactly that invisible. Credentials are never handled by the tooling: for a private repo the bootstrap uses whatever auth already exists on the machine and, failing, prints the three real options (read-only deploy key, ssh -A agent forwarding, gh auth login) -- it never asks for or transports a token, and the access probe runs with GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 and ssh BatchMode because a prompt in a non-interactive SSH session hangs rather than fails.
data.title: Cluster nodes run with Postgres and Redis explicitly disabled

data.rationale: P0: comparison_stats could never produce a p-value. app/blueprints/comparison/routes.py:619-620 built group_labels AND subject_ids as the same expression [t[animal_pos] for t in idx.tolist()], so group == subject for every row; compare_groups pivots subject x group, every off-diagonal cell is NaN, paired_wilcoxon_tests drops every pair and dependent_omnibus_test gets len(complete)==0. The card always reported 'Wilcoxon skipped; insufficient paired subjects' regardless of data. Decision (user, 2026-07-22): comparison must support BOTH shapes - single dataset vs single dataset, and group vs group. group_labels is therefore derived from the selection the user made in <ba-filter mode=multi>: when named groups are selected, the label is the group name; when individual datasets are selected, each dataset key is its own label. subject_ids stays the ANIMAL in both shapes. Consequence to surface honestly rather than hide: a single-dataset-per-group comparison has one subject per group, so paired/repeated-measures tests are undefined - the card must say WHY the test is unavailable and offer the unpaired alternative, not silently emit the same 'insufficient paired subjects' string it emits today. This is the same fact R7.1 surfaces as the single-dataset-group warning.
data.title: Comparison group labels come from the USER SELECTION (single datasets or named groups), never from the animal id

data.rationale: sciCORE is a single machine, so it gets a single block. The connection (host, transfer_host, user, key_path, known_hosts, timeouts) used to sit in a separate `compute.ssh:`, so answering 'how do I reach the cluster?' meant reading two places -- a SLURM host IS an SSH host with a scheduler on top. `ssh:` is merged in and removed; app/services/compute_hosts.py::_inherited_settings still reads a legacy `ssh:` block first so an older config keeps working. The loose run settings (cpus_per_task, mem_per_cpu, time, array_throttle) moved under `slurm.default_run:` because they are the FALLBACK for an analysis with no template in configs/slurm/, not a machine cap. At the top level every machine inherited them, which handed every analysis the same generic 8 cores and silently defeated the per-analysis templates -- a 2-core summary billing for 8. Related: machines are NAMED BLOCKS under compute: (see ba-dec-named-machine-blocks), not a `hosts:` list.
data.title: compute.slurm is ONE machine: connection + scheduler + default_run

data.rationale: There was no slurm, hardware or ssh configuration anywhere in pipeline.yaml, so nothing could route a run to the cluster. compute: now holds default_target, local.max_parallel_jobs, slurm.* (account donafl00, partition, the sciCORE qos_ladder as an ordered name/max_hours list, cpus_per_task, mem_per_cpu 3G, time, array_throttle, remote_venv, remote_data_root, remote_scratch) and ssh.* (host, transfer_host, user, key_path, known_hosts, timeouts). It exists to be read by the hardware page (machines + resource usage), the pipeline page (choosing a target) and the running page (queue + job state). This only became cheap to add once the translator routed by namespace -- per-leaf mapping is why it was absent. Config comments record the two traps: sciCORE compute nodes have NO internet, and the HPC-visible NAS mount Z:\Sergej\Steffen_Experiments is NOT the same share as U:. Secrets stay out per ba-rule-no-secrets-in-pipeline-yaml -- key PATHS only, asserted by a test that greps the committed file for password/passphrase/secret/token and for key material.
data.title: configs/pipeline.yaml gains a compute: section (local | slurm | ssh)

data.rationale: basic_analysis/config/translate.py mapped a single semantic LEAF to a dotted physical path, one _PARAM_MAP row at a time. Adding one option meant editing the translator, which is exactly why whole subtrees (slurm, ssh, hardware) were simply missing from the config -- the cost of adding them was N hand-written rows. _PREFIX_MAP now maps a namespace to a physical namespace with LONGEST-PREFIX-WINS; exact _PARAM_MAP rows still take precedence over any prefix. A new leaf under a mapped namespace (another suite2p op, another slurm key) needs NO translator edit. Public helpers: physical_path(key) returns the resolved dotted path or None, register_prefixes(mapping) adds namespaces at runtime (mirroring the existing register_params). cfg_get's KeyError now names both escape hatches. Gotcha found while doing this: leaving a stale exact _PARAM_MAP row pointing at the OLD physical path silently beats the new prefix -- the exact-match check runs first, so a move means DELETING the old rows, not just adding the prefix.
data.title: Config translator routes by NAMESPACE prefix, not one row per leaf

data.rationale: The Excel workbook (1409 rows x 50 cols, 35 animals) is the source of truth for experiment metadata; the old pipeline exported it to YAML with column names hardcoded in Python (yaml_creator.py), so renaming a column meant editing code. The new parser takes its column map from configs/pipeline.yaml and loads straight into Postgres with Redis caching. That is the ORIGIN of the hardcoded 30 Hz sample rate downstream. Exactly three messy numeric columns (duration [min] 30 bad incl. '20+', depth 79, weight [g] 45) are reported for curation, never silently rewritten. YAML is kept as the parity oracle until every field is reproduced from the sheet. data.rationale: Docker cannot run on the sciCORE login node (user-confirmed) -- normal for HPC, since Docker needs a root-equivalent daemon that no shared cluster grants. The HPC-native path is Apptainer, which sciCORE supports and which runs OCI/Docker images rootlessly INSIDE a SLURM allocation. Model ExecEnvironment as a per-host strategy ORTHOGONAL to JobBackend: JobBackend = where a job is scheduled (local thread vs SLURM), ExecEnvironment = what wraps the python command (venv | apptainer | docker). Keeping them separate avoids a combinatorial SlurmDockerBackend/SlurmVenvBackend mess; it resolves to a command PREFIX and nothing else changes. Because compute nodes have no internet, a .sif cannot be pulled at job start -- it must be built ahead on a login/transfer node and staged, so venv (uv is first-class on sciCORE; .venv on the shared FS is visible to every compute node) is what runs today. Ship venv first; add apptainer when reproducibility demands it. Never silently fall back from apptainer to venv -- a run you believe was containerised but wasn't destroys the reproducibility the container was for.
data.title: Containers on the cluster are Apptainer inside a SLURM job; SSH+venv is the fallback and the day-one default

Documented in docs/src/analysis/statistics.md with the honest caveat that comparing many analyses by eye is itself multiple comparison and this rule does not protect against it. The MI card reports corrected AND uncorrected significant-cell counts side by side.
data.title: Multiple-comparison family = one analysis; never across analyses or runs

data.rationale: PROTOTYPED AND PROVEN 2026-07-17 against a copy of the real 584 MB output/video/master.h5: detect legacy in 0.001s (read-only), migrate 584,070,536 -> 65,235,231 B (88.8% smaller) in 0.98s, second call a no-op in 0.001s, 12 subsequent rewrites FLAT (62.67/63.13 MiB oscillation), no leftover temp files, source untouched. ENABLER: the setting is readable back from Python -- f.id.get_create_plist().get_file_space_strategy() returns (strategy, persist, threshold) and index 1 (persist) is the discriminator (0=legacy, 1=managed). Because that check is a ~1 ms read-only open, ensure_freespace_managed(MASTER_H5) can be called at every app startup and batch entry point and then forgotten -- no maintenance action, no button, no cron. API: freespace_is_managed(path) -> bool; ensure_freespace_managed(path) -> bool (idempotent). Migration runs UNDER hdf5_write_lock with a re-check inside the lock (TOCTOU), verifies content equality (inventory + NaN-aware byte-compare of every dataset) BEFORE swapping, keeps a .premigrate.bak (removed on success, kept on failure), and uses os.replace for an atomic swap. Only dependency is h5py, already pinned. CAVEAT: the first migration is O(file size) and holds the write lock for its duration (~1s at 584 MB); if the master ever reaches tens of GB, move it behind an explicit action rather than inline at startup.
data.title: The free-space fix is fully automated in pure h5py -- no h5repack, no extra packages, no cron

data.rationale: WHAT GEL DRYING IS (corrected by the user 2026-07-23, after an earlier wrong reading): it is NOT a global downward/upward trend across the recording. The drying gel forms bubbles or similar local disturbances that move, so it affects SPECIFIC CELLS SCATTERED ACROSS THE FIELD OF VIEW. A scattered spatial pattern is therefore the EXPECTED signature, not evidence that the detector is firing on noise, and a local-run detector is the right shape of algorithm. Do not 'fix' the counter by making it a global trend test, and do not treat Mann-Kendall (a global rank-trend test) as the more correct detector - it is a different question. THE BUG THAT WAS REAL: detect_gel_drying reported 'cont. increase' but counted CUMULATIVE rises - not_bad_counter (the dip tolerance) was reset by every rise, so in noisy data it never reached its ~929-step budget while bad_counter incremented on ~half of all steps. Measured: flat Gaussian noise with zero trend gave 0/8 cells at 2-3 min but 8/8 at 5, 10 and 30 min; real data gave 120/120. Letting dips accumulate instead was tried and REJECTED - it lost a genuine 10-minute ramp and broke the existing test that isolated dips must not wipe a real rise. The accepted fix requires a run to also go somewhere: the mean at the end must exceed the mean it started from by more than the noise floor, the anchor being LOCAL to the run (which is correct for a local phenomenon). After: flat noise 0/8 at every duration, ramps 8/8 at 5 and 10 min, real data ~5.5% of cells scattered across 6 recordings / 3241 cells.
data.title: Gel-drying counter must require net progress, not just rising steps

data.rationale: gpu_concurrency x cpu_threads_per_worker are STRUCTURAL - they bound how much work is dispatched and cannot react to anything else on the machine. The four CPU/GPU percentage caps only make sense as FEEDBACK limits, and nothing sampled load at all, so they were dead for weeks. ResourceGovernor adds the feedback loop: non-blocking psutil (5.2 ms vs 1010 ms blocking), time-constant EWMA with tau=25 s because sampling is lazy and gaps range from seconds to a 1719 s suite2p stage, max blocks / target releases. Replaying real series proved the two mechanisms fix DIFFERENT failures: on a noisy series at the ceiling a plain threshold flips 11/12, EWMA alone still flips 5, deadband alone flips 0; but on a single 100% spike on an idle machine the deadband alone still throttles and only the EWMA prevents it. Smoothing alone is NOT sufficient. Blocks are bounded at 300 s - a campaign that silently stops forever is worse than one running slowly, and it is the failure that reads as a hang. reserve_cores was DELETED not implemented: wrong currency (4 of 32 cores = 87.5%, inside the existing 80-95 deadband), and an affinity mask does not reserve cores for the desktop, it only forbids the campaign from using idle ones.
data.title: Structural limits cap dispatch; only a feedback limit can respond to load

data.rationale: The workstation is a desktop, not a compute node. Unbounded, two video workers put the RTX 3060 at 97% with 11922 of 12288 MiB consumed and each worker held 11.7 GB RSS and 131 THREADS, because OpenCV fans one decode across all 32 cores. A worker count cannot fix this: the video and imaging legs are separate processes and neither can see the other's GPU use. gpu_concurrency is therefore enforced by N LOCK FILES (not a counter) so a killed worker releases its slot when the OS drops the handle - this campaign is killed routinely and a counter would leak a slot every time. cpu_threads_per_worker must set OPENCV/OMP/MKL/NUMEXPR/OPENBLAS/VECLIB together AND call cv2.setNumThreads; capping only OMP leaves OpenCV free to take the machine. Config lives at hardware.local.resource_limits.
data.title: Bound campaign GPU/CPU with a cross-process semaphore, not worker counts

data.title: The GPU Apptainer container DOES work on WSL2 (with the driver bind)

data.rationale: MEASURED 2026-07-17 (h5py 3.16.0 / HDF5 2.0.0), reproducing the repo's exact write pattern (create tmp -> move old to bak -> move tmp into place -> delete bak) across SEPARATE open/close cycles: default strategy grows LINEARLY, 30 rewrites of one 0.78 MiB dataset -> 23.50 MiB (30.1x bloat); fs_strategy='fsm', fs_persist=True, fs_threshold=1 stays FLAT at 1.57 MiB (2.0x, which is just old+new coexisting during the move). 93.3% smaller and it stops growing. CAUSE: HDF5 tracks freed space only IN MEMORY for the lifetime of the open file and does not persist a free-space manager; this repo opens/closes the store once per write, so every close forgets the free list and the next write appends. Migration proven: repacking the bloated default file into an fsm file gave 24,639,272 -> 822,928 B and stayed flat through 10 further rewrites. CONSTRAINT: fs_strategy is settable ONLY at file creation (passing it on 'a' of an existing file is a silent no-op), hence the one-time repack. Superblock v0 -> v2 (readable by HDF5 >= 1.8, 2009) so compatibility cost is nil. REJECTED: repack-after-every-edit -- it is O(file size) per write, holds the exclusive lock for its whole duration, doubles peak disk, and treats the symptom.
data.title: Stop HDF5 bloat at the source with a persistent free-space manager; repack ONCE, never per-edit

data.rationale: HDF5 permits many concurrent readers; what is unsafe (without SWMR, declined in ba-dec-no-swmr-single-writer) is a reader running concurrently with a writer, which can observe torn metadata mid-B-tree-update. Plan 02 Task 5 originally gave readers master_store_lock -- a plain alias for the EXCLUSIVE write lock -- which serialised readers against each other for no safety benefit and stalled the web app behind a long ingest. hdf5_read_lock (shared, filelock.ReadWriteLock) now backs reads and the write path takes the same lock's exclusive mode so the two genuinely interlock. Two subtleties found by testing, not reasoning: is_singleton=False is required because a singleton tracks the held mode on the INSTANCE not per thread, so a reader thread hit 'downgrade not allowed' instead of blocking; and a read nested inside a write must be a thread-local pass-through since ReadWriteLock forbids write->read downgrade. Measured: 3 readers concurrent, a reader blocks ~0.3s behind a 0.4s writer. tests/test_hdf5_rw_lock.py pins both exclusion directions.
data.title: HDF5 readers share a lock; only writers are exclusive

data.title: Issue #16 'groups not detected' root cause: sheet write-back skipped disk-ingested animals

data.rationale: USER INSTRUCTION: do not freeze a computed number into the config. 'auto' derives from the recording's MEASURED sample rate - 5/10/10/19 frames at 15/30/30.9668/60 Hz. It resolves to a DURATION (0.32 s), never a frame count, so nothing recording-specific is frozen and the version hash does not change between rates. Precedence: explicit min_width_event (frames) > explicit min_width_s (seconds) > auto. Writing a number in the config OVERRIDES the automation, and that is the documented escape hatch rather than a bug. A test asserts the shipped config value is not a bare number, so nobody can re-freeze it. This matters because the corpus runs at 30.9668/30.9710 Hz, never 30.0 - a 30 Hz-derived integer would be silently wrong.
data.title: min_width_s ships as 'auto', resolving to a duration not a frame count

data.rationale: Three parallel stores existed for the same idea: POST /api/groups writes a fixed member list to the sessions.groups JSONB, app/static/saved_views.js keeps a named restorable snapshot behind the header bookmark, and the request was to name a filter and make a group out of it. Decision: a named filter is a live DatasetQuery in a new Postgres saved_filters table (JSONB query + schema_version) that re-evaluates as the corpus grows; a group is a one-way FROZEN materialisation of that query into sessions.groups with the originating query recorded as provenance. They are different objects and both exist. saved_views.js is DELETED and absorbed, because shipping a third store is the fragmentation this change exists to end. Groups stay frozen because comparison statistics need a stable cohort - a group that silently gains members between two runs makes results irreproducible. query is JSONB precisely so a filter over a field that does not exist yet stores without a migration; on read, a predicate naming an unregistered field is dropped with a visible warning rather than failing the whole query. DELETE /api/groups/<name> already exists at app/blueprints/groups/routes.py:137 and is called from nowhere - it finally gets a UI.
data.title: A named filter is a LIVE query; a group is a FROZEN snapshot; saved views are absorbed into named filters

data.rationale: `compute:` already described machines before the /hardware page existed -- `local:` is one. Saving from the page invented a `compute.hosts:` LIST that restated everything `slurm:`/`ssh:` already said: account, partition, remote_venv, host, transfer_host, key_path and both timeouts appeared twice, in two shapes, free to drift. A machine is now `compute.<name>:` in the existing style, so adding a WSL box writes a `wsl-ubuntu:` block beside `local:`. A machine inherits from the shared blocks and only its own DIFFERING values are written (app/services/compute_hosts.py::machines_to_config), so the duplication cannot return. Reserved keys (slurm, ssh, local, default_target, hosts) are never touched by the writer and a machine may not take one of those names -- it would shadow the settings. A legacy `hosts:` list is still READ so nobody loses machines. Of everything in the duplicated block exactly one value was not stated elsewhere -- `user: mauser00` -- which was migrated into the slurm block rather than dropped.
data.title: Machines are named blocks under compute:, never a parallel hosts: list

data.rationale: Confirmed: sciCORE compute nodes have the shared filesystem but NO internet; only the login node has outside network access. So: compute nodes read raw input over the share and each task writes ONE PRIVATE staging file (X.h5.partial -> atomic rename to X.h5). Single-writer-single-file over NFS is safe -- NFS locking is only dangerous for CONCURRENT access to ONE file, which never happens here, so the design sidesteps the NFS-locking problem rather than fighting it. Compute nodes never touch the master, never take a lock, never need egress. The workstation is the single writer into a LOCAL master (the Z: drive share Sergej/Steffen_Experiments and /mnt/f/Experiments/Steffen_Experiments are the SAME share, so results need no rsync). The login node's network is for control (sbatch/squeue/sacct/logs), not data. Caveat: if HDF5 hangs writing a staging file on cluster NFS, set HDF5_USE_FILE_LOCKING=FALSE narrowly in the sbatch env for that job only -- safe because each task owns its file exclusively -- NEVER as a Python import side effect.
data.title: The shared NFS/SMB share is a transport for private staging files; the master HDF5 stays local to one machine

data.rationale: CONFIRMED: sciCORE compute nodes have NFS access to the experiment data. Z:/Sergej/Steffen_Experiments (workstation) and /mnt/f/Experiments/Steffen_Experiments (cluster) are the SAME share. data.strategy: mount is therefore the default for sciCORE and the following are DROPPED, not deferred: the rsync stage manifest (path -> size,mtime,hash), input-set derivation per run plan, the 1 TB soft-quota guard, the 301 GB / 5,260 .npy transfer via transfer12, and staging cost as a factor in auto host selection (the data is equidistant). Results need no transfer either: a compute node writes its staging file onto the share and the workstation's drain reads it in place -- no tar, no scp. No bulk data crosses the VPN; the tunnel carries only SSH control traffic. 'stage' remains a config strategy for a FUTURE host with no shared mount, but must not be built until such a host exists. SUPERSEDES the earlier claim that compute nodes cannot mount the share, which was inferred from what the public docs DESCRIBE rather than from what the cluster DOES -- public documentation is evidence of what is documented, not of what exists. STILL TRUE: the master HDF5 must never live on the mount (flock unreliable over NFS/SMB), and compute nodes still have no internet.
data.title: sciCORE compute nodes mount the data share; the stage-in half of Plan 08 is deleted

data.rationale: Once a public key is in authorized_keys, SSH is challenge-response: the private key never leaves the machine and no password crosses the wire. The only use for a stored password was the one-time key bootstrap, not worth a dependency or a store. paramiko was added then removed.
data.title: No encrypted credential store and no paramiko; key auth ends the password need

data.rationale: sciCORE is a shared university facility: unowned, unrooted, already scheduled by SLURM, and its compute nodes have no internet egress. k8s cannot be installed there, would duplicate SLURM where it could, and the owned fleet (~1 workstation) is too small to schedule. Apptainer is the supported container seam inside a SLURM allocation. Datadog needs a per-host agent that can neither be installed on compute nodes nor phone home, bills per host, and would duplicate sacct/seff which are free. Use: sacct/seff for cluster jobs, hardware.html (escalate to Prometheus/Grafana at ~5+ owned hosts), Sentry for app errors (workstation only).
data.title: No Kubernetes, no Datadog; SLURM accounting + hardware page + Sentry

data.rationale: HDF5 is already 2.0.0 (h5py 3.16.0), so the >=1.10 requirement is long met and no version work is needed. SWMR is still wrong here on four independent grounds: (1) it forbids creating objects after entering SWMR mode, but the result-store contract creates a group per analysis and uses f.move() (result_store.py:449,458,473-474), which SWMR cannot express; (2) SWMR is single-writer while the actual defect was multi-writer; (3) files are created libver ('earliest','v200'), not 'latest'; (4) SWMR does not work over NFS/SMB. The existing staging.py + auto_merge design (private per-run files, one writer merging under the lock) is already correct -- the work is to enforce it, not replace it.
data.title: No SWMR; keep single-writer + staging + merge

data.rationale: MEASURED + PROBED 2026-07-17. Of 5,260 .npy files under F:/Experiments/Steffen/Intrinsic_Imaging, only 527 (10.0%) were ever written into any HDF5 (525 cell_drying + 2 cell_metadata), and ZERO are in output/video/master.h5 which app/config.py:9 hardcodes as the app's store. Probe of that store: top level ['animals'] only; recordings/S1 -> ['analysis']; contains fluor:0 upphase:0 detrended:0 stat:0 velocity:0 is_wheel:0 sttc:0 corr:0 index:0 cell_drying:0. S1 has no activity dataset, so add_recording was never called -- the 584 MB is video frame tables (from MP4 via video/pipeline.py) plus cached analysis results (result_store.py:137). build_store_from_npy (master_hdf5.py:1542) is DEAD CODE, referenced only by tests, and obsolete (hardcodes fps=30.0 at :1630 while 520 fps.npy files exist). Its successor rebuild_master_store (master_hdf5.py:1817, CLI scripts/management/rebuild_master_store.py:37) is the correct foundation and has NEVER been run against the live store. The reader side already exists and waits: load_fluor_step:717 reads fluor/<version>/<step>, finds no fluor group, falls back to .npy at :820. This is the FOURTH instance of the repo's recurring pattern -- infrastructure built for a consumer that never arrived (use_sql_query, the chunks table, /index/recordings, now the ingest path).
data.title: The .npy corpus is NOT ingested: 10% overall, 0% in the store the web app reads

data.rationale: Ported from the proven legacy shape in SERBRA/Examples/Scicore/structure_index: a .cmd manifest with ONE LINE PER UNIT OF WORK, submitted once as `sbatch --array=1-N%K`, where each task selects its own line with `sed -n "${SLURM_ARRAY_TASK_ID}p"`. One static template plus a text file -- no per-job scripts. Verified on the real corpus: 1425 planned tasks -> 1425 manifest lines -> `sbatch --array=1-1425%20`. TWO PROPERTIES CARRY THE CORRECTNESS. (1) The LINE NUMBER IS THE TASK ID: comments and blanks are stripped before numbering, and app/services/slurm_array.py::manifest_lines mirrors exactly what the shell does, so 'which dataset is task N?' has one answer. If a comment counted, inserting one would repoint every task at a different recording and the array would run, succeed, and analyse the wrong data -- nothing would report it. Never reorder or delete manifest lines while an array is queued. (2) One MUnit per task keyed by its REAL id, never merged and never a positional index, with the MEASURED fps travelling on the line (the suite2p runner refuses to start without fs, and this corpus has three distinct rates). The template also pins OMP/MKL/OPENBLAS/NUMBA to SLURM_CPUS_PER_TASK: unpinned, those libraries size themselves from the NODE's core count (128 on a scicore node), so an 8-core allocation spawns 128 threads that thrash each other -- slower than serial, and billed for the full walltime.
data.title: One SLURM array task per dataset, driven by a .cmd manifest

data.rationale: CORRECTION to the premise that pipeline.html already represents present data. flow.html's card border colours come from the hand-authored _SKELETON node state (active/planned/blocked, graph.py:59-197) = IMPLEMENTATION STATUS, and flow.js:75 literally calls it 'mock availability'. The only real HDF5 probe is _plot_provenance (graph.py:282-372), which reads actual partition attrs 'so the edge cannot drift from the stored result' but SYNTHESIZES silently when absent. So reuse _open_store (graph.py:375) and the provenance-probe shape; do NOT copy the card-colour mechanism believing it reports data presence. UI: overview.html already calls dataset_statistics(MASTER_H5, DATA_DIR) (overview/routes.py:45-49) -- both sources already in hand -- and already has an animal x date heatmap with a selectable aspect (routes.py:52-57). Presence becomes aspect='presence': one enum value, the existing filter bar, an idiom users already read; a parallel presence panel would be the worse UI and the worse code. Tri-state fill + GLYPH (hue is never the only channel), per-kind tooltip with resolved h5/disk paths, a summary line, and a legend stating amber = works-but-un-ingested, not broken. Batch the probe: one store open per matrix, not per cell -- overview_stats.py:85 is the cautionary tale and this page is where it would recur at 520 dates x N kinds.
data.title: Data presence is an aspect of the EXISTING overview heatmap, not a new widget; pipeline.html does not already show it

data.rationale: The column rendered metadata provenance from corpus_sources.SOURCE_ORDER (database/excel/csv/folder structure/missing data), which is a different axis from where a dataset physically lives. Worse, SOURCE_ORDER ranks 'database' first and resolve() is an if/else, so any session with a usable Postgres row is labelled 'database' and never 'excel' - and the scan itself fills that Postgres row from the sheet, so the label degrades toward 'database' over successive scans and ERASES the origin it was meant to report. Decision: the user-facing column becomes multi-label presence (nas / staging / processed / excel); the 'database' label is dropped; provenance is not deleted but moves to a per-row detail view. MISSING DATA moves out of the source column into the modalities column where absence of data actually belongs. The presence axis is realised as basic_analysis/io/presence.py, the ba-presence-resolver component the graph already records as planned, rather than as a parallel concept.
data.title: The overview source column shows data PRESENCE (nas/staging/processed/excel), not metadata provenance

data.rationale: Memory moved out of the shared `memory` graph into a dedicated `basic-analysis` graph declared in agent-skills cluster.yaml, so an overwrite or bad write in another project cannot touch it. .mcp.json pins OMNIGRAPH_GRAPH_ID=basic-analysis; a second `omnigraph-globals` server exposes the shared `memory` graph, because the MCP bridge is pinned to one graph via env var and none of its tools take a graph argument -- reading both project memory and global-scope Preferences therefore needs two servers. Migrated 2026-07-16 with infra/mcp-servers/scripts/split-project-graph.py: 95 nodes / 99 edges copied; source `memory` left intact.
data.title: basic-analysis memory lives in its own Omnigraph graph (per-project isolation)

data.rationale: Paths describe THIS machine: raw_nas_root is a `U:` drive letter that exists only on the workstation, data_dir and master_hdf5 are local filesystem locations, and a cluster host carries its own data_root/run_root. Keeping them top-level implied they were machine-independent, which is how a local drive letter came to be quoted at a cluster that cannot see it. About a dozen call sites read cfg['paths'][...] raw (scripts/, nb_common, the loader's own defaulting), so basic_analysis/config/loader.py::_project_local_paths PROJECTS the canonical block back to a top-level `paths` key -- a shallow copy, so a caller mutating cfg['paths'] cannot rewrite the canonical block, and the canonical home wins if a config somehow has both. The translator prefix points at compute.local.paths and the stale exact `paths.*` _PARAM_MAP rows were DELETED: an exact row beats a prefix, so leaving one would have silently kept resolving to the old location (the same trap the suite2p move hit). Reached further than expected: config_schema.REQUIRED_SECTIONS required a top-level `paths` (now `compute`), and five curated help entries orphaned -- caught by the same guard that caught the suite2p move.
data.title: configs/pipeline.yaml `paths:` moved under compute.local

data.rationale: A named volume ALREADY survives container recreation -- `down`/`up` and `docker rm -f` never touched basic-analysis_ba_pgdata, so the premise 'move it so it is not lost when the container is recreated' was wrong. What a named volume does NOT survive is `docker compose down -v`, `docker volume rm`, and a Docker Desktop factory reset; and it cannot be backed up with the arrays because it lives inside the WSL2 docker-desktop-data VHDX on C: where nothing else looks. Bind-mounting ../../output/pgdata fixes both: the cluster sits beside the master.h5 whose arrays its rows point at, `-v` now only drops the disposable Redis cache, and output/ is gitignored so it cannot be committed. The relative host path resolves against the compose file's OWN directory (Compose's project-directory default), so it lands at <repo>/output/pgdata from any invoking cwd -- confirmed with `docker compose config`. Postgres-on-a-Windows-bind-mount was TESTED, not assumed: the widely-reported initdb 'could not change permissions ... Operation not permitted' failure did NOT reproduce here -- initdb, restart-against-existing-cluster and a write/read roundtrip all passed in a throwaway container before live data was touched. Perf is a non-issue: the cluster is ~9 MB and fits entirely in the default 128 MB shared_buffers, so steady-state reads never reach the slower virtiofs path. Migration was dump/restore (not a raw copy) and verified by exact COUNT(*) per table before and after: analysis_index 512, animals 10, cell_labels 509, cells 890, job_runs 0, qc_masks 2, recordings 191, sessions 128, store_provenance 703. Redis deliberately stays on a named volume -- it is a rebuildable cache, never a source of truth. The old basic-analysis_ba_pgdata volume was left in place as a rollback point and is now stale.
data.title: The Postgres cluster is a bind mount at output/pgdata, not a Docker named volume

data.rationale: Two detectors, two questions. Gel drying = a LOCAL RUN of rising windowed mean from a bubble moving across the FOV; scattered cells are the EXPECTED signature and the counter is CORRECT (~5.5%). Mann-Kendall = a monotone DECLINE across the whole recording, i.e. a fading or dying cell. I previously called MK the better drying detector - that was WRONG. The old MK code was unusable as a bleach test: it blocks by MEAN, so a cell that merely FIRES LESS trends down and gets called bleaching; new detector uses the 20th percentile per block. KEY MEASUREMENT: 46% of all cells show a statistically significant monotone decline after Hamed-Rao and BH, so a p-value-only label would flag half the corpus. The MAGNITUDE GATE (>=0.5%/min), not the p-value, is what makes the test safe - on phase-randomised surrogates the full gate flags 0.000% while raw MK flags 8-31%. Shipped rate: 2.02% of 8169 cells, but 0.0% in 12 of 19 recordings and 24.5% in the worst, because bleaching is a property of the RECORDING as much as of the cell. ANNOTATE, never exclude by default: excluding fights the cell-identity requirement, and dropping cells does not fix a bleached session, it removes the evidence it differs.
data.title: Mann-Kendall's real job is photobleaching, not gel drying - and it annotates, never excludes

data.rationale: MEASURED against the real npm artifact 2026-07-17 (plotly.js 3.7.0), not estimated: plotly.js-dist-min = 4,854,193 B (4.6 MiB, mostly gl3d/mapbox); plotly.js-cartesian-dist-min = 1,427,455 B, the js itself 1,424,820 B (1.36 MiB) <- USE THIS; plotly.js-basic-dist-min = 1,122,409 B but LACKS box + heatmap so it is unusable here. The proposal's ~3 MB estimate was ~2x pessimistic. Trace types extracted from the minified source: bar, box, contour, heatmap, histogram, histogram2d, histogram2dcontour, image, pie, scatter, scatterternary, violin -- covers every renderer the repo has. Pinned sha256 7c593b9eda0e74a1d07335cf89cbf7a55ffc114909980c3729af835453bdb02a. THE STRONGEST ARGUMENT, WHICH THE PROPOSAL MISSED: there are ZERO log axes today (grep -c for Math.log|log10|logScale|'log' in plots.js returns 0) while the repo runs neuronal-avalanche/criticality POWER-LAW analysis (analysis/maxent/avalanche.py, criticality.py). A power law is read on log-log axes, so the web cannot currently draw the plot the science requires -- it is matplotlib-only. That is a capability gap, not ergonomics. REJECTED PREMISE: plotly does NOT fix the two-renderer divergence -- after migrating you still have plotly (web) + matplotlib (visualization/statistics_plots.py, publication). Unifying those means giving up scienceplots/vector-PDF or adding kaleido, a separate larger decision. The divergence was caught by a human noticing, not by a test, so the real fix is making the discipline machine-checkable. Vendored not CDN (offline lab machines/VPN), loaded as a plain script BEFORE the ES modules (module scripts are implicitly deferred, so a classic tag always defines window.Plotly first; no defer/async).
data.title: Migrate the WEB plotting layer to Plotly (cartesian bundle); matplotlib stays for publication

data.rationale: Ingest writes Postgres first via upsert_session, so a metadata-store failure is visible rather than masked by the mirror succeeding; never fatal, because an ingest must not abort when the metadata service is down (logs WARNING, returns False). The HDF5 scalar (write_session_fps) is kept only so an installation without Postgres still resolves a rate. get_sample_rate reads a final on-disk fps.npy tier because most of the corpus is un-ingested and without it every rate-scaling analysis refuses to run on raw data -- it is a measurement the store has not caught up with. Verified 2026-07-23: the existing data is CLEAN -- Postgres holds 685 sessions, 669 with fps, every value in [30.9668, 30.971] and not one 30.0; the HDF5 stores carry 3 fps attrs, all 30.9668. So no re-ingest is needed. Implements ba-rule-sample-rate-measured-or-null.
data.title: Postgres holds the frame rate; the HDF5 scalar is a legacy mirror; fps.npy is a transitional read tier

data.rationale: Measured 2026-07-16: list_datasets on the 584 MB app store costs 1.3 ms; dataset_tree (a filesystem crawl of F:) costs 94.6 ms. The HDF5 open is 1.4% of the request -- an HDF5-metadata index optimises the fast half. The data root holds ZERO .h5 (301 GB / 7,706 files, 5,260 .npy); HDF5 is the derived output cache, not the corpus. Scale is 10^2 rows vs SQLite's ~50k / DuckDB's ~10^7 / Postgres' concurrent-writer thresholds. The real defect is an N+1 at overview_stats.py:85/355 (525 opens of a 584 MB file), fixed by hoisting a with statement. The old neural-analysis stack showed no gain not because of the NVMe but because its query path (use_sql_query io.py:743, chunks table 0 rows) was never connected. Revisit only for a genuinely multi-writer run store -- a concurrency argument, not a query-speed one.
data.title: PostgreSQL + Redis declined; fix the N+1 instead

data.rationale: Plan 17. Pure numeric arrays stay in HDF5; descriptive/run metadata, the analysis catalog and the job store move to PostgreSQL; Redis is a read-through cache, job-status bus and cross-machine lock. Every path degrades gracefully: Redis down falls through to Postgres, Postgres down falls through to HDF5/filesystem, so nothing hard-requires a service. Supersedes the earlier decline (ba-dec-postgres-redis-declined) because the multi-machine/concurrency trigger that decision itself named has now fired. The real speed win is moving the catalog into Postgres so the overview stops crawling the filesystem (measured 94.6ms of a 95ms request); Redis only caches that. Dedicated containers: basic-analysis-postgres :5433, basic-analysis-redis :6380, credentials in a tracked .env (private repo).
data.title: Split HDF5 arrays from Postgres metadata; Redis as an optional accelerator

data.rationale: Three states: in_master (serve from HDF5), on_disk (serve, cache, WARN), absent (raise DataNotAvailableError -- never None/empty). Absence must raise because silent fallback is exactly how 'the ingest never ran' went unnoticed: load_fluor_step:717 finds no fluor group and quietly falls back to .npy at :820; load_gel_drying_mask:1043 quietly takes the disk-only branch. A missing input is a bug, not an empty plot, and must never be silently equivalent to 'zero cells'. ONE resolver (basic_analysis/io/presence.py::resolve) is consumed by BOTH the read path and overview.html -- if the page probed separately the two would drift and the page would show green for data the loader cannot read. Logging: fallback at WARNING (not DEBUG), JSON-lines via Plan 06's formatter, plus an {in_master,on_disk,absent} counter; warn once per (kind,animal,date,rec) per run, not per call (~20 specs re-read the same array, so per-call would emit 20 identical warnings and train everyone to ignore them). SEQUENCING: caching requires the store-path unification (ba-dec-unify-master-store-path) first -- until then ship cache=False, because a cache written to the file the app does not read is worse than no cache: it looks like it worked. That is literally how 525 cell_drying masks became inert.
data.title: One resolver decides where every datum comes from; absence RAISES; the overview page renders its answer

data.rationale: rebuild_master_store fed F_detrended.npy into the store AS the raw step, then the dF/F step divided it by its own median. A detrended trace is centred, so that median is ~zero: measured std 33 where 0.045 is correct. EVERY store built from the legacy .npy corpus is affected - that is the 525-session corpus behind the first 33 figures. Root cause is vocabulary, not arithmetic: the codebase used 'raw' and 'fluorescence' interchangeably. USER RULING 2026-07-23: 'raw' must hold the actual raw trace and nothing else; the word 'fluorescence' in an analysis context means F_detrended - filtered and detrended, but NOT binarized. If the legacy corpus has no true raw trace, mark it absent rather than substituting the detrended one. Guard: a near-zero median is detectable, so dividing by it must raise and name the recording rather than silently producing a 700x-wrong scale.
data.title: 'raw' must be the real raw trace; 'fluorescence' for analysis means F_detrended

data.rationale: Cross-check 2026-07-22: 0 of 512 analysis_index h5_path values and 0 of 703 store_provenance rows resolve inside output/master.h5, nor in output/analysis.h5, output/video/master.h5 or the newest backup; only qc_masks resolve (4/4). All were written in one 18-minute window (2026-07-20 11:26-11:44 UTC) by a run whose HDF5 output did not survive. The catalog claims 128 dataset_keys x 4 analyses all status='ok', while master.h5 holds real analysis groups for exactly ONE session (DON-017115/20231123) which has NO analysis_index row. Decision (user, 2026-07-22): RE-INGEST rather than delete. Two parts: (1) scripts/db/reconcile_pointers.py marks unresolvable rows status='missing' - a new CHECK value - so the store stops asserting 'ok' about arrays that do not exist, and nothing downstream trusts them in the meantime; (2) the marked rows drive a re-ingest run that recomputes and rewrites the arrays. Also fix the cause: master_hdf5 must write the provenance row only AFTER the dataset write commits, so a failed or discarded write can never leave a pointer behind. The re-ingest compute itself is hours of work and is launched by the user, not by the web app.
data.title: The 1215 dangling Postgres pointers are re-ingested, not deleted

data.rationale: Re-running an analysis invalidates only the data-generating stages — suite2p, cell QC, gel-drying, behavior video — not derived read-only analyses. Prevents a re-run from silently discarding downstream results the user still wants, while still forcing regeneration of the expensive upstream artifacts.
data.title: Re-run clears only data-generating stages

data.rationale: Default ROIs computed from frame size: paw = full LOWER HALF (paw motion energy), pupil = TOP-LEFT corner, twitch = ~50x50 box at CENTRE. Each ROI name is drawn in a distinct colour for fast visual separation. A Save button stages an edit and sets a needs-re-run flag; while set, any analysis depending on that ROI is BLOCKED until the ROI analysis is re-run, which clears the flag -- so an accidental ROI change cannot silently produce wrong results. The ROI edit also carries a manual-annotated flag distinguishing it from an automatic default.
data.title: A video-ROI edit gates dependent analysis until re-run; defaults are per-body-part, colour-coded

data.rationale: app/services/request_guard.py inspects POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE only. 'most of the benefit for a fraction of the work' of CSRF tokens (which would touch every fetch() in the UI). Two counter-intuitive rules carry it: Sec-Fetch-Site: none is ALLOWED (a hostile page cannot cause it -- the header is a forbidden header name script may not set), and an ABSENT header is ALLOWED (refusing breaks curl, the repo scripts and ~1200 tests while stopping nothing, since a client choosing its own headers can send same-origin). Override BA_ALLOW_CROSS_ORIGIN. Known gap: DNS rebinding -- a hostile hostname pointing at 127.0.0.1 is same-origin in the browser's own view; the fix is a Host allowlist, deliberately not implemented while the app stays on loopback. See web-app-security-posture memory.
data.title: Same-origin Sec-Fetch-Site guard instead of CSRF tokens for the loopback single-user app

data.rationale: `sacctmgr show assoc user=$USER` was finally run on the cluster and returned: Cluster=scicore, Account=donafl00, User=mauser00, Def QOS=6hours, QOS list including 1day/1week/2weeks. This closes the single fact that gated every submission: `donafl00` had been INFERRED FROM A DEAD REPO since the start and never confirmed, and a wrong --account is rejected outright rather than queued. CRITICAL DISTINCTION, now pinned by a test: `account` is the BILLING account (donafl00) and is NOT the username (mauser00). A request came in to rename account->user; doing so would have put mauser00 into `#SBATCH --account` and had every job rejected. The two are different fields and both are required. Recorded in configs/pipeline.yaml under compute.slurm with `cluster` and `default_qos` as well, both settable per machine on /hardware.
data.title: sciCORE credentials VERIFIED LIVE — account donafl00, user mauser00, Def QOS 6hours

data.rationale: Evicting whole Session objects frees nothing: clearing animal.sessions left 24/24 arrays alive, because any live caller (the batch's pair list, a spec, a route) still references them. The eviction unit is the individual array, keyed (session token, array name); the token is a monotonic counter not id(session) because ids are reused after collection. Budget is fraction * (available_RAM + already_cached) -- the + already_cached term is load-bearing, since without it every cached byte lowers available, which lowers the budget, which evicts, converging on an empty cache on any machine. psutil is soft-imported (not a core dep). 230 MB and rising -> 57.6 MB flat from session 4. Reported-not-fixed: session_loader.load_session_data() still reads ~144 MB to use 0.24 MB per session in loops (behavior_coupling.py, video/batch.py).
data.title: Per-array LRU bounded by available RAM, not per-Session eviction

data.rationale: User decision. Bernoulli gave Fano 0.667 at the shipped defaults and 0.0 when peak_rate >= sample_rate (silent saturation: every in-field frame a guaranteed spike). Poisson measures 0.997. Bernoulli remains reachable via model='bernoulli' and now RAISES rather than silently clipping when the rate cannot be represented. Matters disproportionately because synthetic data is what the analysis code is validated against -- a wrong generator makes every analysis that passes on it inherit the error. Part of the simulation-package audit (docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-22-audit-remediation/AUDIT-simulation.md). Calcium amplitude/SNR deliberately NOT changed: the audit's GCaMP6f reference figures were the auditor's own recollection and need checking against the lab's indicator characterisation first.
data.title: rates_to_spikes is Poisson by default; Bernoulli is opt-in and refuses to clip

data.rationale: basic_analysis/analysis/maxent/slurm/ holds the repo's best SLURM tooling (seff EXIT trap, config-driven renderer, cmd-grid generator, rerun generator) -- strictly better than anything in the three legacy repos -- but is invisible under maxent/, which is why the top-level slurm/ tree drifted into a stale copy of neural-graphs with two incompatible memory dialects (--mem vs --mem-per-cpu). Promote it to a top-level orchestration package so there is a single source of responsibility, and make configs/pipeline.yaml carry all connection/resource information (account, qos, hosts, roots).
data.title: SLURM/orchestration code moves out of analysis/maxent/slurm to a top-level package

data.rationale: Every #SBATCH directive is an sbatch CLI flag that overrides it, so generating scripts buys nothing and costs reviewability, testability and drift -- the stale --array=1-2 in slurm/graphs/ is that drift already realised. Commit one reviewed slurm/templates/analysis_array.sh; keep generate_cmd_grid.py (generating .cmd DATA is right, generating SCRIPTS is not). Map one session per array task with --cpus-per-task=1 and pinned OMP/OPENBLAS/MKL thread vars: a 128-core whole-node job (precompute_sttc_arrays.sh:11-13) bills full core-walltime for one straggler, queues for a whole node, and loses all N sessions on one crash. Persist the sbatch argv on the job record as the provenance the generated .sh used to provide.
data.title: One committed sbatch template + array jobs; one session per task

data.rationale: Optical spillover is a property of a PAIR of ROIs (touching or overlapping contours), not of a cell, so the gate drops the pair and keeps both cells - quality_control.exclude_spillover_cells is false because removing suspect cells decimates dense fields of view. The fill value must be NaN, not 0: a substituted zero is still averaged in and drags the mean correlation toward zero, manufacturing exactly the reduction the gate exists to test for. exclude_suspect_pairs lives in analysis/spatial_qc.py; gate_similarity's 0.0 stays correct for graph adjacency, where 0 means 'no edge'. Before this, neither compute_pairwise_correlations nor matrix_spike_time_tiling_coefficient excluded suspect pairs at all - the stored mask had exactly one consumer (graph adjacency).
data.title: Spillover is gated per PAIR with NaN, never per cell and never with zero

data.rationale: recordings is UNIQUE(session_id, subsession) with ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE. A human-mislabelled session YAML (session_parts ['S2','S2']) made the second S2 overwrite the first -- DON-009191/20220302 stored one row at 55,748 frames where the array has 111,496 (half the session silently gone). Raw data intact; the store lost a row. Ingest now detects the collision and renumbers sequentially (preferring the .mesc filename's S1-S2), with a loud warning.
data.title: Duplicate sub-session labels are renumbered at ingest so no recording is lost

data.rationale: Measured 2026-07-22: Postgres recordings.subsession is S1..S6 while the disk fallback basic_analysis/io/layout._subs_from_split_recordings:323-340 emits wheel_1 / platform_1, and of 520 comparable sessions EXACTLY ONE agrees. A naive DB-disk union inflates the tree from 1422 to 2436 entries and a wrong positional guess silently opens the WRONG recording under a correct-looking label, which is a data-integrity failure rather than a UI bug. Decision: a recording id is the canonical ^S\d+$ form only when Postgres or HDF5 supplies one; disk names are carried as aliases only when counts agree and canonical ids already exist, otherwise they become their own rows with sources.db=false. The UI renders 'S1 . platform_1'. A filesystem path is NEVER derived from S<n> alone - layout.stored_rec() and layout.video_path() remain the only path builders. This makes a mismatch visible instead of silent and degrades to a real mapping later if the acquisition order is ever confirmed.
data.title: Never map Postgres S<n> onto disk wheel_1/platform_1 positionally; carry both labels instead

data.rationale: suite2p.ops.fs was 30. There is no honest default: output already on disk carries 10.0 Hz (a merged run), 30 (per-MUnit) and 30.9668 Hz, and the real rate is measured per recording from the .mesc header (ZAxisConversionConversionLinearScale -> ~30.9668 Hz). fs sets BOTH the temporal binning for cell detection AND the deconvolution timebase, so a wrong value rescales every rate, STTC window and criticality number downstream -- silently. The config now ships fs: null meaning 'use the measured rate'; a number is an override for data with no .mesc and warns. The flip side is that the runner must SAY SO rather than hand None to suite2p: basic_analysis/pipeline/suite2p_run.py::run_suite2p_subsession raises ValueError when ops['fs'] is missing or None, naming the three real on-disk rates. _DEFAULT_OPS (the standalone packaged fallback) also carries fs=None. This is the suite2p-side instance of ba-rule-sample-rate-never-hardcoded.
data.title: suite2p ops fs is null -- the measured per-recording rate, never a default

data.rationale: The repo orchestrates suite2p per subsession, configured via a standard ops file, ported from AnimalClass. Verified current state: io/suite2p.py + preprocessing/io.py only load/parse suite2p outputs — the runner is ABSENT (a verified gap). Plan 04.
data.title: Run suite2p per subsession via a standard ops file (not on a merged mask)

data.rationale: configs/pipeline.yaml had suite2p split in two: the RUN PARAMS under imaging.suite2p_ops, the orchestration (ops_file, per_subsession, dedup, geldrying, binarization) under suite2p:. 'Where do I set tau?' therefore had two plausible answers, and imaging: was carrying things that are not optics. Everything suite2p now lives under suite2p.ops / suite2p.ops_overrides; imaging: keeps only fov_um_per_px and fov_um_per_px_overrides. imaging.suite2p_ops.* still RESOLVES via the translator alias so old callers keep working, but it is no longer a physical key. Two consumers had to follow the move: basic_analysis/io/calibration.py::resolve_suite2p_ops read cfg['imaging']['suite2p_ops'] by RAW DICT ACCESS (bypassing the translator), so the move would have made it silently return {} and suite2p would have run on library defaults with nothing reporting it -- it now goes through _suite2p_block, which falls back to the old literal location for config FILES still written the old way; and six curated help entries in app/services/config_help.py orphaned, caught immediately by the repo's own guard test_curated_keys_reference_real_yaml_paths. Pinned by tests/basic_analysis/config/test_config_modularity.py.
data.title: suite2p has one config home: suite2p.ops (was split across imaging.suite2p_ops)

data.rationale: tau is suite2p's sensor decay timescale in seconds, driving the deconvolution kernel. suite2p's own convention: 0.7 = GCaMP6f, 1.0 = GCaMP6m, 1.25-1.5 = GCaMP6s. This project images GCaMP6f, so the previous 1.0 was simply the wrong indicator's constant -- it over-smoothed deconvolution and blurred fast transients. Set to 0.7 in configs/pipeline.yaml suite2p.ops.tau and in the packaged _DEFAULT_OPS fallback. Two other ops were added at the same time: block_size [128,128] (non-rigid registration tiles, powers of 2 for FFT efficiency, roughly FOV/4 for a 512px FOV) and functional_chan null (null = take the session YAML's channel; the 2022 two-channel cohort needs 2, and running detection on the structural channel yields cells with no dynamics).
data.title: suite2p tau = 0.7 (GCaMP6f), was 1.0 (the GCaMP6m value)

data.rationale: Measured 2026-07-22: Postgres holds 35 animals / 673 sessions / 1422 recordings; output/master.h5 holds 31 animals; GET /api/datasets/tree returns FIVE animals because require_video defaults True at app/blueprints/workspace/routes.py:120 and the shared filler app/static/scope_init.js:69 hardcodes the URL parameterless, so /neural, /clustering and /pipeline inherit a gate chosen for /behavior. Decision: GET /api/datasets/catalog backed by app/services/dataset_catalog.py unions Postgres (identity, sex/dob/pnd, groups) with the disk scan (always require_video=False) and the master HDF5, returns rows + faceted counts + the normalised query in one round trip, and exposes video presence as a per-row sources flag rather than a discovery gate. Per ba-rule-redis-never-source-of-truth no tier is required: a dead tier logs once, contributes [], and sets tiers.<x>=unavailable. format=tree emits the legacy {animal:{date:[sub]}} shape so migration is incremental. Supersedes /global/metadata/session_table, which does not exist in the live store, rather than reviving it.
data.title: One registry-driven dataset catalog endpoint replaces eight scope layers over three discovery stacks

data.rationale: local said data_dir/plotting_dir while slurm said remote_data_root/remote_scratch/container at machine level -- four names for two concepts, which made _PARAM_MAP confusing. Now data_root is read-from, run_root written-to, container run-inside, identical for local/wsl/slurm. Legacy spellings resolve through exact _PARAM_MAP rows and the loader re-adds data_dir/plotting_dir for the dozen raw cfg[paths] readers.
data.title: Every machine has a uniform paths: sub-block (data_root/run_root/container)

data.rationale: app/config.py:9 hardcodes MASTER_H5 = BASE_DIR/output/video/master.h5 and IGNORES paths.master_hdf5 (configs/pipeline.yaml:41), which basic_analysis/io/dataset.py:960 resolves via get_path(). Probed consequence: output/master.h5 holds 525 qc/cell_drying nodes; output/video/master.h5 holds 0. dataset.py's caching writes land in the batch store while the web app reads the video store, so the cache is written and never read. NEITHER file is a superset -- the video store has all the video tables + analysis cache, the batch store has the 525 masks -- so unification requires a merge (store_merge/auto_merge) and an explicit decision about which physical file survives. This also violates the config-SSOT constraint the 2026-07-08 overhaul README pins. Until this lands, EVERY caching fix writes to a file the app does not read.
data.title: app/config.py must resolve the master store from config; two divergent stores make every cache inert

data.rationale: USER RULING 2026-07-23, overturning ba-dec-binarization-input-not-parameters' reading. The specification is C:\Users\mauls\Documents\Code\binarize2pcalcium\legacy\secondversion.py, binarize_folder lines 194-216: f0=|median(F)|; dff=(F-f0)/f0; F_filt=lowpass(dff, high_cutoff, order=1); F_det=detrend(F_filt, mode_window=900); thresholds=find_threshold(F_det[k]) DETRENDED; F_on=binarize_onphase(F_det) DETRENDED; F_up=binarize_upphase(F_filt, F_det) with signal FILTERED and gradient DETRENDED. binarize_upphase(traces, traces_grad) takes the two arrays SEPARATELY - it thresholds `traces` and takes np.gradient(traces_grad) - so the split is deliberate and must not be collapsed onto one array. binarize2pcalcium/pipeline.py:268 agrees. Our docs/src/binarization_validation.md section 10.1 argued the opposite (that calcium.py:1517 rebinds F_filtered to the detrended array so upphase is post-detrend) and pipeline.py:349 passed F_detrended; section 10.1 is being corrected. WHY THE EVIDENCE LOOKED CONTRADICTORY: the 100.0000%-frame-exact replay that appeared to confirm the detrended reading necessarily fed F_detrended as BOTH signal and gradient, because secondversion.py saves F_raw/DFF/F_detrended/F_onphase/F_upphase but NEVER F_filtered - the one array it binarizes is the one array not persisted. That replay therefore constrains everything downstream of the detrend but cannot distinguish the two hypotheses. COMPARABILITY WITH LEGACY FIGURES IS EXPLICITLY WAIVED by the user - the project is in strong development and all figures may be recreated. Also ruled: F_detrended can carry negative values (it is centred by the polynomial detrend plus the 900-frame mode subtraction) so it must be used with caution; and raw + dff + filtered + detrended are ALL to be persisted in the HDF5 store, which is what stops this ambiguity recurring.
data.title: The upphase binarizer thresholds F_filtered; F_detrended supplies only the gradient

data.rationale: basic_analysis/analysis/behavior_coupling.py::_raw_behavior_traces looked for `velocity.npy`. The file is `merged_velocity.npy` -- the name io/session_loader.py, io/velocity.py, analysis/behavior_states.py and io/master_hdf5.py all use, and the only one on disk. The lookup has a three-step fallback (loader method -> attribute -> file), but Session exposes NEITHER load_wheel_velocity() nor .wheel_velocity, so the filename was the only route. It always missed, behavior_signals substituted an all-zero trace by design (`a signal the session does not provide is returned as an all-zero trace`), and every wheel-velocity coupling result was computed against a fabricated stationary animal. Nothing raised. The existing test wrote `velocity.npy` too -- it was written from the code rather than from the data, so code and test agreed and it passed. Verified on DON-017115/20231113: None before, 74320 samples (max 0.146 m/s) after. GENERAL LESSON: a 'missing -> neutral default' fallback converts a wrong path into a plausible result, so the fallback needs a test written against REAL on-disk filenames, not against the code. Surfaced but not fixed: merged_velocity.npy is session-scoped and ~50% trailing NaN (the non-wheel portion), which now propagates through np.interp instead of being masked -- deliberately not coerced to 0, recorded in manual-todo.md.

data.statement: Two layers prevent simultaneous HDF5 writes and BOTH must stay: (1) basic_analysis.io.hdf5_lock.hdf5_write_lock (filelock + in-process RLock) is ADVISORY -- it only constrains code that calls it; (2) HDF5's own OS-level file lock is what makes an accidental parallel write IMPOSSIBLE, turning a silent corruption into a hard OSError. Never disable (2) to work around (1). For the batched merge drain the unit that holds the lock is the BATCH: one acquire -> open the master once -> merge as many staging files as the budget allows -> close+flush -> release -> delete merged files -> repeat if any remain. Releasing between batches is required for reader correctness, not politeness: an unbounded hold makes every cross-process read fail with OSError for the duration (D5).

min_width_event for the upphase/onphase binarizers must be DERIVED FROM THE SAMPLE RATE, never a fixed integer. The reference implementation (AnimalClass manifolds/donlabtools/utils/calcium/calcium.py, set_default_parameters_2p) defines min_width_event_upphase = sample_rate // 4 (0.25 s) and min_width_event_onphase = sample_rate // 2 (0.5 s), with min_thresh_std_upphase = 1.5. A hardcoded 7 is only correct at exactly 30 Hz; these recordings run at 30.9668 / 30.9710 Hz. A hardcoded value produced 92-96% silent cells on real data, which is how the bug surfaced.

Before trusting any constant in a legacy reference script, grep for EVERY assignment to it - this codebase has twice been misled by a value set early and silently overwritten later (high_cutoff 1->0.5, min_width_event sample_rate//4 -> 10). Last assignment wins. Also check whether the argument carrying it is commented out at the call site, which makes it dead code that survives only as output metadata.

A config key that no code reads back is a BUG, not a placeholder: it reads as configured behaviour that does not exist. Shipped three times now - gpu_memory_floor_mb, then five CPU/GPU percentage caps that had no sampling loop at all while CPU sat at 98.1% against max_cpu_percent 95. A new key must land in the SAME change as the code that consumes it. Where a declared key is not yet wired, mark it 'not enforced' on the row in any UI that shows it, not in a tooltip, and pin the unenforced set in a test.

Any setting in configs/pipeline.yaml under compute.{local,slurm,ssh} that describes A MACHINE must also be a HOST_FIELDS entry and have a FIELDS entry in app/static/hardware.js, so it is editable per machine on /hardware. The failure this prevents is silent: a setting works for the global block while being invisible and unsettable on every machine card. Six were in exactly that state (transfer_host, known_hosts, connect_timeout_s, command_timeout_s, max_parallel_jobs, description). Enforced by tests/app/services/test_compute_hosts.py::test_every_machine_setting_in_the_config_is_a_host_field, which walks the real config, counts nested mappings too, and requires any exclusion to be justified in _NOT_A_HOST_FIELD (currently qos_ladder -- a site-wide menu, not a machine value -- and compute.local.paths -- local filesystem locations whose per-machine equivalents are data_root/run_root). Verified non-vacuous by injecting compute.ssh.proxy_jump and watching it fail.

No compute function reads a raw nested YAML path; all config access goes through the translator seam (basic_analysis/config/translate.py), which mirrors app/services/h5_paths.py::resolve_group. As of 2026-07-20 the translator maps at TWO granularities: _PARAM_MAP (exact semantic leaf -> dotted physical path, checked first) and _PREFIX_MAP (semantic namespace -> physical namespace, longest prefix wins). Prefer a prefix so a new leaf needs no translator edit. When a section MOVES, delete its stale exact rows -- an exact row pointing at the old path silently beats the new prefix. Raw dict access is the failure mode this rule exists to prevent: resolve_suite2p_ops read cfg['imaging']['suite2p_ops'] directly and would have silently returned {} when the section moved.

app/services/pipeline_config_writer.py owns `compute.hosts` and NOTHING else in configs/pipeline.yaml. It was written when `compute:` meant hosts alone: _render emitted {"hosts": [...]} and the splice replaced the entire `compute:` line span, so the moment sibling keys (default_target/local/slurm/ssh) were added, the first Save on /hardware silently deleted them -- cluster account included, without which every SLURM job is rejected at submission. The splice is now scoped to the `hosts:` sub-block via _find_hosts_span. Before adding any key under a section a web page can write, check what that page's writer re-renders: a block-level splice destroys every sibling it does not know about, and the failure is silent because the file still parses. Pinned by tests/app/services/test_pipeline_config_writer.py::TestComputeSiblingsSurvive and test_hardware_page.py::test_save_does_not_disturb_the_rest_of_the_config.

Every fitting routine ships a parameter-recovery test against known ground truth (corrcoef(fit, true) > 0.9), not merely a self-consistency check. LEARNED FROM: the MaxEnt MPF objective was sign-inverted -- it fitted the ANTI-model, driving data states to high energy -- and EVERY existing MPF test passed, because they checked finite differences OF THE CODE'S OWN COST, symmetry and determinism, all of which hold under an inverted sign. maxent/synthesize.py had produced h_true/J_true for free the whole time and nothing compared against them. A fit that is never scored against known parameters is not tested, however many assertions surround it. See tests-that-cannot-fail memory and AUDIT-maxent.md.
