The suite2p functional channel is a PER-SESSION fact. Authoritative source: <corpus>/animals.yaml at {animal_id}:sessions:{date}:fucntional_channel (misspelling is real). Measured over 685 sessions: 591 ch1, 15 ch2, 25 None, 54 absent; absent/None means channel 1. Only 3 animals ever use ch2 (DON-008497 one day, DON-009191, DON-009192) and it flips mid-animal: DON-009192 runs 2 -> 1 -> 2 -> 1 -> 2, being ch1 on 20220327-29 BETWEEN two ch2 stretches, so no date interpolation is valid. Do NOT generalise 'a two-channel file needs channel 2' - that is false and was stated in error. ROOT CAUSE OF THE UNRELIABILITY: fucntional_channel == n_channel in ALL 606 populated entries, so the field encodes the CONVENTION 'the functional channel is the last one acquired', not a measurement - it is therefore wrong wherever a session allocated two channels and filled only one. Hence the record must be checked against the pixels. Two real sessions fail in OPPOSITE directions: DON-008497/20220130 records ch2 but its Channel_1 is a flat constant 1536 (std 0.0000) while Channel_0 has std 160.22; DON-009191/20220215 records ch2 correctly and its Channel_0 is the flat one. Record-only and probe-only are both insufficient - always call select_functional_channel (which does both), never resolve_functional_channel alone.

A synthetic-data test must assert the STATISTIC the generator exists to produce (the avalanche exponent, the Fano factor, the lattice peak distance), not just array shape or finiteness. LEARNED FROM: in tests/basic_analysis/simulation/, test_poisson_rate_consistency had a tolerance 3x its expected value (an all-zeros array passed); the supercritical branching test passed on sparse noise AND on a solid block of ones (the generator was stuck in an absorbing all-active state); test_bursty_spikes_shape passed on an array that was 99.99% zeros -- and it was. Across the whole simulation package exactly THREE tests could have failed if a generator broke. Ask 'what would this still pass on?' -- if the answer includes all-zeros, all-ones or pure noise, it asserts nothing. See tests-that-cannot-fail memory.
A single global, config-definable random seed is set and honoured everywhere for reproducibility.

Never claim HDF5 file bloat or 'real data size' from data.nbytes (that is in-memory size of what was read; for object/vlen dtypes size*8 counts POINTERS) or from get_storage_size() alone (it EXCLUDES the global heaps holding vlen string payloads). The only unambiguous test is repack-and-compare: copy every object into a fresh file and diff the sizes, then verify content equality (group/dataset/attr inventory + byte-compare) before trusting the result. Measured 2026-07-17: output/video/master.h5 557.0 MiB -> 62.2 MiB repacked (88.8% reclaimable, 0.2s), content byte-identical across all 406 datasets.
No overclaiming: 'putative twitch' (the state gate is an EMG-free surrogate) and drift-without-position uses proxies only with mandatory bleaching controls.

A multi-agent wave that rewrites a bounded set of files MUST run in its own git worktree, not in the shared checkout. Measured 2026-07-23 on Wave 2 of the web-UI unification: two sessions edited app/static/components/ba-filter*.js simultaneously and the wave could not converge. app/static/components/ba-filter.js went 593 -> 713 -> 670 -> 642 -> 611 -> 637 lines DURING two fix rounds; ba-filter-help.js (279 lines) and ba-filter-modal.js (231 lines) appeared from the other session mid-task and were never created by this one. The wave's own design-SS9 line-budget test then failed against lines the other session added (ba-filter.js 637 and ba-filter-view.js 627 against a 600 cap), and a test written by the other session (ba_filter_modes.test.mjs asserting hex group colours) failed against this session's change to var(--group-N) - each session's verification measuring the other's in-flight edits. Symptoms to recognise: a verification lens failing on a metric nobody in your wave changed; files appearing in your owned set that your agents did not create; a file's line count moving between two reads in the same task. Cost when ignored: unbounded fix rounds that never converge, plus commits that sweep in a third party's unfinished work (Wave 0 had to be staged by explicit path for exactly this reason, and a concurrent session's dropped _proc_lock re-export in app/services/result_store.py broke collection of tests/app/services/ for hours). Use superpowers:using-git-worktrees, or serialise the waves. Waves 0 and 1, whose file sets no other session touched, converged without this problem.

Analysis results and dataset arrays must be load-if-cached from the master HDF5 (keyed by dataset+QC+fluor_version+params via result_store get_or_compute / read_result_partition); recompute only on a genuine cache miss. Batch and web paths must share one partition scheme; a compute-called-once test must guard it.

NEVER DELETE OR MODIFY ANYTHING ON THE NAS STORAGE (U:\RG Donato\..., and any other NAS-backed path). The NAS holds the ONLY copy of the raw experimental data - .mesc imaging files and .mp4 behaviour videos that cannot be re-acquired. It is READ-ONLY, without exception. This covers: deleting files, moving or renaming them, writing into NAS directories, and any --apply mode that could reach a NAS path. Staging copies on H: may be deleted once their analysis is recorded as done; the NAS source never may. Any script with a delete or reap capability must assert its target is NOT under the NAS root before acting, and must fail closed if it cannot determine the root. If a task appears to require deleting from the NAS, it is a misunderstanding - stop and ask. User instruction 2026-07-23, stated with maximum emphasis.

No module may set HDF5_USE_FILE_LOCKING (esp. =FALSE) at import. It disables HDF5's cross-process lock for the WHOLE process, is import-order dependent (setting it after import h5py is a no-op), and turns silent corruption into the default. Enforced by tests/test_hdf5_locking_not_disabled.py (AST scan of basic_analysis/**, app/**, notebooks/**). If a lock conflict appears, fix the conflicting writer -- the error is the bug surfacing.

Never wrap a lookup whose empty answer is legitimate in `except Exception`. LEARNED FROM (twice in one session, 2026-07-23): a `except Exception: return None` around an fps-on-disk lookup turned a NameError (missing Path import) into 'no rate on disk', which is indistinguishable from the legitimate absent case, so the bug was invisible; and the same pattern in a Postgres-write helper. Catch only what a BAD INPUT can raise (OSError/ValueError/IndexError/TypeError) and WARN rather than staying silent. A broad except around a lookup whose empty answer is normal hides every bug in that lookup. Worth a repo-wide sweep of app/** and basic_analysis/** for bare `except Exception: pass`.

configs/pipeline.yaml must never contain a password, key material, or token -- SSH hosts carry a key PATH only; passphrases go to ssh-agent or an env var. pipeline.yaml is committed. Likewise SSH must use RejectPolicy with explicit user approval of an unknown host key, never AutoAddPolicy.

The per-session YAML metadata files WILL BE DELETED. No runtime analysis path may read them. animals.yaml is an INGEST-TIME source only, read by scripts/management/sync_functional_channel.py to populate the Excel sheet and Postgres. The runtime resolver chain is DB -> sheet -> config default -> 1, with no YAML step. A chain that falls back to YAML is a future outage, not a safety net.

All heavy compute is parallelized via numba (CPU) or torch (GPU) and ships a benchmark test proving a significant speedup (clustering, geometry, topology + nulls, decoders, twitch, tracking, drift, correlations/STTC).

A PATH export written for remote/batch use must go in ~/.profile, not only ~/.bashrc. Ubuntu's stock ~/.bashrc RETURNS EARLY for non-interactive shells, so a line appended there never runs under `ssh host command` or `bash -lc` -- which is exactly how a SLURM job or a remote submission invokes things, and the failure looks like a broken install ('command not found') rather than an unset PATH. scripts/cluster/install_apptainer.sh writes ~/.profile first (creating it if absent) and .bashrc/.zshrc/.bash_profile as well for interactive use. Verified with `bash -lc "apptainer --version"`.

A bind mount is not a backup. output/pgdata survives a deleted CONTAINER; it does not survive a cluster corrupted by an unclean shutdown, an `rm -rf output/pgdata`, or a move to a newer Postgres major. Take logical dumps too: scripts/db/backup.py writes output/backups/pg-<ts>.dump (~60 kB -- arrays are in HDF5, so only metadata is in scope) and prunes to the newest --keep (default 7), the same rotation app/services/auto_merge.py applies to master-<ts>.h5. The app's AUTO_BACKUP thread covers ONLY the HDF5 store, so without this the arrays are backed up and the catalog pointing into them is not. Three implementation invariants: (1) pg_dump runs INSIDE the container -- this workstation has no host pg_dump/psql, and an in-container client is guaranteed to match the server version; (2) credentials are read from the container's own environment via `sh -c`, never passed on the host command line, so they stay out of the process list (same discipline scripts/db/bootstrap.py uses for the role password); (3) dumps are written to a .part file and renamed only on exit 0, so an interrupted run cannot leave a truncated file that looks valid. The restore path must be exercised against a THROWAWAY container (BA_PG_CONTAINER override) rather than trusted -- an untested restore is not a backup.

If the Plotly cartesian bundle is adopted, the no-violin rule MUST be machine-enforced, because the bundle registers `violin` and drawing one becomes `type:'violin'` -- one word -- where today it would take ~200 lines of canvas nobody writes by accident. Enforce twice: (1) the shared draw() helper in app/static/plotly_theme.js throws on any trace with type==='violin'; (2) a source scan test fails on type:'violin' anywhere in app/static/*.js. Distributions are `type:'box'` with `boxpoints:'all'` (boxplot WITH scattered points). See ba-conv-boxplots-not-violins.

Every plot must state which fluorescence version the analysis ran on - the content hash AND the human-readable step name (raw/dff/filtered/detrended), because a bare hash tells a reader nothing. Follow the existing annotate_channel precedent in basic_analysis/visualization/figures/channel_provenance.py rather than inventing a second provenance mechanism. Rationale: four persisted stages now exist and the binarization input changed on 2026-07-23, so a figure that does not name its input cannot be interpreted or reproduced.

In a git worktree, preview_start reads the MAIN repo's .claude/launch.json and starts servers with the MAIN repo cwd - so the default dev server silently serves a DIFFERENT checkout than the one being edited, and verification passes against code you did not write. Add a launch entry that chdirs into the worktree and inserts it on sys.path. Also: plain navigate to a localhost origin is REFUSED; preview_start({url}) works and returns navOk true.

Prove the READ path on a stopwatch before merging the WRITE path. The repo has four instances of infrastructure built for a consumer that never arrived: use_sql_query (old neural-analysis repo, io.py:743), its chunks table (0 rows ever), /index/recordings (master_hdf5.py:1486 -- implemented, never populated, never read), and the whole .npy ingest path (build_store_from_npy dead + rebuild_master_store never run, while load_fluor_step:717 waits for a fluor group that does not exist). Corollary: never claim a loop is a performance problem without verifying it EXECUTES -- overview_stats.py:85's 525-open N+1 is gated on `if not df.empty` and its session_table does not exist in either store, so it is dead code, not a hot path.

Results under different QC / dataset-selection / fluor-version go to separate master.h5 partitions; any change to the frame/cell filter creates a new results partition recording the exact frames + cells + results.

Redis is never a source of truth - it is only a cache, bus and lock. Every value held in Redis must be reconstructable from Postgres or HDF5, and no code path may hard-require Redis or Postgres: a missing service logs once at WARNING, returns None, and falls through to the next tier.

A recording's frame rate comes from its own measurement, or it does not exist. fps.npy -> Postgres sessions.fps / HDF5 .../fps is the only source. There is NO fallback -- not a literal in code, and (since 2026-07-23) not preprocessing.sample_rate in configs/pipeline.yaml, which was the 'only permitted fallback' and is now merely the rig's nominal rate, valid only where no recording is in scope (synthetic data, ms->frame bin conversion). RENAMES ba-rule-sample-rate-never-hardcoded: 'never hardcoded' was satisfiable by a config-sourced guess, which is exactly the loophole this closes. (1) resolve_sample_rate(session) returns None when no measurement exists, warning once PER SESSION where the absence is discovered (a single global latch left the second unrated session of a batch unmentioned). (2) Anything that scales by time calls require_sample_rate(session), raising SampleRateUnknownError naming the session and the fix -- an analysis that cannot know its rate must refuse to run, not produce a plausible wrong number. All 22 call sites were migrated; without that they receive None and raise a bare TypeError deep in arithmetic, worse than the guess it replaced. (3) Nothing may PERSIST a rate it did not measure: None survives as NULL/NaN through add_recording, list_recordings, /index/recordings, write_session_fps and the Postgres mirror, so a stored value always means 'measured'. write_session_fps deliberately does not DELETE an existing value -- a re-ingest that lost its fps.npy must not wipe an earlier correct measurement. (4) Never read session.sample_rate directly -- it is None until resolved; enforced by tests/app/test_sample_rate_never_bypassed.py (AST scan of app/**). VERIFIED 2026-07-23: existing data is clean -- Postgres holds 685 sessions, 669 with fps, every value in [30.9668, 30.971] and not one 30.0; the HDF5 stores carry 3 fps attrs, all 30.9668. The fabrication path existed in code but was never exercised at scale, so no re-ingest is needed.

The sample/frame rate must never be a literal in code. The real per-recording rate (fps.npy, and in future the sheet's fps [Hz]) is authoritative; the only permitted fallback is configs/pipeline.yaml preprocessing.sample_rate, and falling back must WARN once, because a session recorded at 30.97 Hz but scored at 30.0 silently corrupts every rate, tuning and criticality number derived from it.

Shell scripts, Dockerfiles and YAML must keep LF endings, pinned by .gitattributes (`*.sh text eol=lf`). On a Windows checkout git converts LF->CRLF and bash then dies on the FIRST line with `set: pipefail\r: invalid option name`, which reads as a broken script rather than a line-ending problem. These files execute on Linux (cluster login nodes, WSL, CI), so the working copy must stay LF too. Found by running scripts/cluster/install_apptainer.sh under WSL rather than reading it.

Every plot and every test attaches a comparison-to-shuffle null; the test type, its reasoning and n_shuffles appear in the plot legend and are saved to the master HDF5. paired-vs-independent lives in config.

Every writer of a shared HDF5 store must serialise on basic_analysis.io.hdf5_lock.hdf5_write_lock(path). HDF5 has no multi-writer support: two live write handles with independent metadata caches both flush and diverge the superblock/B-tree. Batch/remote results enter through staging + auto_merge (one writer), never by writing the master directly.

Every ROI keeps its stable roi_id in all QC label layers, including cells classified not-a-cell. The cell_qc store holds a roi_ids array plus position-aligned boolean stage arrays (iscell, dry, silent, outlier, spillover, neuropil, bleach, clean) - never a positional cell_index that shifts when cells are added/removed. /api/neural/cell_qc emits cell_index = int(roi_id) with an id_space stamp, so curation edits and label-layer membership always address the same physical cell.
The master HDF5 gives every animal/date/subsession its own isolated space with no spillover â€” no merged-fluorescence-in-place-of-split-data (the current defect being fixed).

An ordinary test run must never read or write the live Postgres/Redis. tests/conftest.py disables both for the session; a test needing a real server opts in with the live_pg / live_redis markers and must skip cleanly when the containers are down. Verified by comparing row counts before and after a run.

Verification and mutation-testing agents must never leave mutations in shared files. Isolate each mutation to a throwaway copy/worktree, and before committing run the full test gate PLUS a byte-identity/residue scan (e.g. no leftover 'if(true){return;}') on every product file touched. A mutation-test artifact once nearly shipped a broken clearVideoSurface in script.js; per the user, pushing a broken file would destroy the repository. Commit per wave and stage only your own hunks. Complements ba-rule-isolate-multi-agent-waves-in-a-worktree.
